title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 112-113): Grothendieck axiomatizes a combinatorial 'analysis situs'. There is a set M of 'figures' with three relations: ≤ (sub-figure), ≪ (a 'relatively compact in' or 'interior' relation) and |o| (read here as 'disjoint' or 'separated'). Mag1-Mag4 are axioms on (M, ≤, ≪, |o|). For X ∈ M, X̃ = {X' ∈ M | X' ≤ X} is the down-set of X.

An 'atelier' (workshop) on M is a family F̃ ⊂ P(M) satisfying:
- AtM1: every Φ ∈ F̃ is ≤-closed (a down-set).
- AtM2: every closed part of a member is a member.
- AtM3: the members cover M, and ∅ ∈ F̃.
- AtM4 (this page): for Φ, Ψ ∈ F̃, Φ ∪ Ψ ∈ F̃ iff every X ∈ Φ and Y ∈ Ψ are compatible (X ≉ Y). Compatibility means: for all X' ∈ X̃ \ (X̃ ∩ Ỹ) and Y' ∈ Ỹ \ (X̃ ∩ Ỹ), X' |o| Y'.

So two figures are compatible when the parts not shared by X and Y are pairwise disjoint. This matches the criterion on p.112 (At3a) for the sup F ∨ G to exist. In effect an atelier encodes how figures can be assembled; members of F̃ are the 'figures' F, which carry the order ≤ via F ↦ F̃.

The atelier is called 'à figures finies' (with finite figures) if the down-sets of its figures are finite. Under axiom 'Mag fin' (∀X ∈ M, X̃ is finite) one then expects F̃ = {Φ finite (closed) ⊂ M | X, Y ∈ Φ ⇒ X ≉ Y}. That is the family of finite down-closed cliques of the compatibility relation: a flag- or clique-complex type structure, built from finite pairwise-consistent configurations.

The sentence 'cela satisfait aux conditions d'un M-atelier sss ...' (this satisfies the conditions of an M-atelier iff ...) is left unfinished.

Closing methodological remark: in this 'algebraic part' it is the atelier that ends up at the centre of the reflection, rather than the set F of all things or figures, which plays a somewhat accessory role.
errors: The formula F̃ = {Φ ∈ P_f(M) | ...} omits the requirement (AtM1) that Φ be ≤-closed. It should read finite down-closed subsets, or else ≉ must be shown to force closure, which it does not.

The characterization 'cela satisfait aux conditions d'un M-atelier sss ...' is left unfinished. The conditions on (M, ≤, |o|) making the clique family satisfy AtM2-AtM4 are not stated. Plausibly some heredity of compatibility under ≤ is needed (if X ≉ Y and X' ≤ X then X' ≉ Y).
AtM4 as an 'iff' requires the pairwise condition to be sufficient for all larger unions too (a 'pairwise implies global' coherence property); this is asserted, not argued.

ideas.what: Axiomatics of an 'atelier': a family of down-closed subsets of a poset of figures, closed under sub-objects, covering, and unions of pairwise compatible members
ideas.modern_name: Configuration domain / coherent family of down-sets; stable domain structure

ideas.what: Compatibility of two figures defined via disjointness of their non-common sub-figures; union of members exists iff they are pairwise compatible
ideas.modern_name: Pairwise consistency implies global consistency (coherence; bounded-completeness / Scott domain)

ideas.what: Mag fin: every figure has finitely many sub-figures; the atelier is then the family of finite down-closed cliques of the compatibility relation
ideas.modern_name: Axiom of finite causes; flag/clique complex of a compatibility graph

ideas.what: Methodological shift: the atelier (the structure of assemblies), not the set of figures, is the central object

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'atelier' axioms closely parallel the configuration theory of prime event structures and Girard's coherence spaces, both from computer science and logic in the same years. The parallels: a poset with finite down-sets ('Mag fin' = finite causes); a binary compatibility relation inherited from sub-figures; admissible families = down-closed, pairwise-compatible subsets; unions existing exactly under pairwise compatibility. No literature appears to link Grothendieck's combinatorial analysis situs to domain theory or event structures.
missed.quote: F̃ = {Φ ∈ P_f(M) | X, Y ∈ Φ ⇒ X ≉ Y} ... Mag fin ∀X ∈ M, X̃ est fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could give a domain-theoretic or 'stable' semantics reading of tame-topology and assembly axioms, and conversely geometric models for coherence spaces. Directed-topology and concurrency work, which already links event structures to cubical complexes, might find a natural ancestor here.

missed.claim: The intended characterization of when the family of finite compatible cliques is an M-atelier (the 'sss ...' clause) is never completed.
missed.quote: mais cela satisfait aux conditions d'un M-atelier sss ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small but well-posed combinatorial question. Completing it would pin down Grothendieck's intended axioms Mag1-4 in the finite case.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary order theory, but the specific shape (finite causes, inherited compatibility, unions of pairwise-compatible down-sets) is strikingly close to event-structure and coherence-space theory, developed independently in the same period. The axiomatics is unpublished and ends unfinished.
transcription_corrections: 'Ah M4' should read 'AtM4' (continuing AtM1-AtM3 from p.112).
The 'sss' at the end of the first line is the abbreviation for 'si et seulement si' (iff), not stray text.
'unigraphes' is a doubtful reading; the word, possibly something like 'ingrédients', seems to refer to the down-sets X̃ (sub-figures) of the figures.
The struck-out first attempt reads roughly 'on a X, Y ∉ Φ∩Ψ, ou X|o|Y', with superscript '{X ≉ Y, i.e.}' inserted.
'Ce rôle un tantinet accessoire' is likely 'joue un rôle un tantinet accessoire'.
The struck-out word before 'Mag fin' looks like 'AtM' or 'AlM'.
